first.rationale: Simplifying onboarding best addresses both the activation and completion declines without the margin and customer-quality risks of reacting immediately with aggressive pricing. Verify memory_86 for the most directly relevant onboarding evidence and memory_73 because promotional pricing is the strongest competing response but its claimed revenue lift may not establish sustainable long-term qualified revenue. A guarded test is appropriate because the inherited onboarding evidence emphasizes early adoption rather than downstream revenue quality.

final.rationale: Run a standard onboarding-simplification experiment. The verified record directly addresses the current completion decline and showed completion +13%, time-to-value improved by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%. Signup simplification also supports likely activation gains. Promotional pricing is rejected despite competitive pressure because verification showed 30-day retention -12% and failure through first renewal, conflicting with sustainable long-term qualified revenue. The experiment should track qualified revenue and retention beyond 30 days because durable revenue impact remains unproven.
